security_audit.summary: The static alerts reflect manual setup steps, placeholder links, Markdown formatting, and game design examples. The README directs users to external prompt checks without explaining data handling and describes a community upstream as official. No evidence found of prompt injection, automatic command execution, or credential collection.

remediation.issue: The external prompt checker is recommended without data handling guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Offer a local checklist first. Explain what the external tool receives and ask users to remove confidential details before sharing prompts.

remediation.issue: The README describes a community upstream as official.
remediation.suggestion: Name the community repository explicitly and distinguish a merged contribution from an endorsement or security review.

content.user_title: Design Game Worlds and Playable Web Showcases
content.value_statement: Game art, cutscenes, and demo pages can drift apart when teams plan them separately. Use shared character references, camera prompts, and web templates to keep them consistent.
actual_capabilities: Draft a character identity profile and a four-view turnaround prompt with consistent proportions, lighting, and wardrobe.
Specify sprite actions and frame counts for idle, movement, abilities, and reactions.
Write cutscene prompts covering opening frame, camera rig, motion, subject tracking, environmental effects, and final frame.
Draft cover art prompts and responsive Tailwind card markup with a clear focal subject and readable badges.
Outline a showcase grid for Canvas and WebGL demos, with optional Web Audio cues and a transition from story to gameplay.
limitations: The package contains guidance and examples, not a built-in image or video renderer.
Prompts can reduce visual inconsistencies but cannot guarantee identical results across generated views or tools.
The game examples describe prototypes; the package does not provide a deployable collection of games.
The card layout suggestions do not guarantee higher click-through rates.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Character Reference
use_cases.description: Define the character features, clothing, and colors that artists should preserve across four views and basic sprite actions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Racing Intro
use_cases.description: Specify how the camera follows a vehicle and where it settles before the race countdown begins.

use_cases.title: Organize a Browser Demo Gallery
use_cases.description: Draft a responsive grid with cover cards, launch controls, and sound settings for existing browser demos.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Character Turnaround
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four-view turnaround prompt for [character concept]. Keep [key features], clothing, proportions, and lighting consistent from every angle.
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a first reference sheet for an original character.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cutscene Shot
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a six-part camera prompt for [scene]. Track [subject] and end on a frame that matches [gameplay view].
prompt_templates.scenario: You know how the scene starts and where the player takes control.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Game Showcase Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a cover art brief and Tailwind card for [game name]. Use [main action] as the focal point and keep the title readable at 320 pixels.
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a card for a responsive browser game gallery.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Integrated Game Showcase
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a character profile, cutscene shot, cover card, and responsive gallery plan for [game concept]. Use [existing demo] and specify launch, mute, and exit behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Your team needs consistent creative assets and a frontend plan for an existing demo.

output_examples.input: Draft a reference and sprite plan for a courier in a yellow raincoat.
output: Keep the yellow raincoat, blue satchel, and short black hair in all four views.
Show front, three-quarter, side, and back views with the same neutral pose and lighting.
Plan a four-frame idle loop and a six-frame run loop.

output_examples.input: Plan a racing intro that leads into the countdown.
output: Open low behind the car with a wide lens, then follow it using a simulated chase rig.
Accelerate through the first turn while keeping the rear lights centered. Show reflections moving across the wet road.
Rise into the gameplay chase view and hold the frame as the countdown appears.

output_examples.input: Outline a gallery for one Canvas demo and one WebGL demo.
output: Stack the cards on mobile and feature the WebGL demo in a wider card on desktop.
Show each title, a readable engine badge, and a Play button.
Keep sound muted until enabled and return visitors to the gallery when they exit a demo.

best_practices: Reuse the same character profile, palette, and lighting description across art and cutscene prompts.
Choose the first gameplay camera view before drafting the cutscene so the final shot matches it.
Test card readability, demo launch, and mute behavior on desktop and mobile before publishing.
anti_patterns: Changing signature features between views while expecting a consistent character.
Starting a cutscene without specifying the tracked subject or final frame.
Submitting unreleased game details to an external prompt checker without verifying how it handles inputs.

faq.question: Can I use only one part of the workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. You can request character design, cutscene prompts, game cards, or showcase architecture separately.

faq.question: What should I provide for a character turnaround?
faq.answer: Describe the role, face, hair, clothing, color palette, and any features that must stay consistent across views.

faq.question: Does the skill render images or video?
faq.answer: It drafts prompts and specifications. Rendering requires a separate image or video tool.

faq.question: Does the package include playable games?
faq.answer: It includes game blueprints, screenshots, and example markup. You must build or supply the games you plan to showcase.

faq.question: Can a showcase include both Canvas and WebGL?
faq.answer: Yes. The layout can present both kinds of demos with links or launch controls.

faq.question: Do I need an external prompt checker?
faq.answer: No. Use the six-part camera checklist to review prompts locally.
